shifts-movements-s1.title: Marlow Street Bakery's busy week
shifts-movements-s1.html: Marlow Street Bakery keeps a graph of its croissant market: price per croissant on the vertical axis, croissants sold per day on the horizontal axis, a downward curve D for its customers and an upward curve S for what it offers. During one week: on Monday the bakery cuts the price of a croissant from $4 to $3. On Tuesday a large office opens next door. On Thursday the butter the bakery buys doubles in price. On Friday a cafe across the street starts selling its own croissants for $2. (An invented bakery.)

curves-crossing-s1.title: A market graph with a shaded triangle and rectangle

items.q: On a market graph in this course, which variable goes on the horizontal axis?
options: The price of the good
The number of sellers
The quantity of the good
The time of year

items.q: A graph has tacos sold per day on the horizontal axis and price per taco on the vertical axis. What does the ordered pair (60, 4) describe?
options: 60 tacos sold at a price of $4
4 tacos sold at a price of $60
A price of $60 for 4 days
64 tacos sold in total

items.q: With tacos sold on the horizontal axis and price on the vertical axis, which ordered pair plots the row for a price of $2?
What relationship between price and tacos sold does the table show?
options: A direct relationship: as the price rises, more tacos are sold
An inverse relationship: as the price rises, fewer tacos are sold
No relationship: tacos sold stay the same
A direct relationship, because both columns hold numbers

items.q: How many more tacos a day does the truck sell at a price of $2 than at a price of $4?

mistakes.why: That adds the two rows. The question asks how many MORE, so subtract the smaller from the larger.

items.q: Which of these points lie on the graph of the table, with tacos sold across and price up? Select all that apply.
Label both axes and both curves of this market graph.
Place point X at a larger quantity and a higher price than the point where the two curves meet.
A part-time worker earns more the more hours she works. If hours go on the horizontal axis and weekly pay on the vertical axis, how do the points look?
options: They fall to the right: an inverse relationship
They rise to the right: a direct relationship
They form a flat line: no relationship
They rise to the left: an inverse relationship

items.q: A student graphs the taco table with price on the horizontal axis and tacos sold on the vertical axis. What is the problem?
options: Nothing: either axis may hold either variable on a market graph
The relationship will change from inverse to direct
The five rows will no longer plot as points
The axes are reversed from the market-graph convention, so the curve will not match the graphs in the course

items.q: A point sits at (0, 7) on a graph with quantity across and price up. Where is it?
options: On the vertical axis, at a price of 7
On the horizontal axis, at a quantity of 7
At the origin, where the axes meet
Off the graph, because 0 is not a value

items.q: Point M is (30, 8) and point N is (50, 6) on a graph with quantity across and price up. Which statement is correct?
options: N shows a smaller quantity and a higher price than M
M and N show the same quantity
N shows a larger quantity and a lower price than M
M shows a larger quantity because its second number is bigger

items.q: What is the slope of a line?
options: The change in the horizontal value divided by the change in the vertical value
The vertical value at the point where the line starts
The change in the vertical value divided by the change in the horizontal value
The sum of the two values at any point on the line

items.q: A straight line passes through (20, 8) and (60, 4). What is its slope?

mistakes.why: That is run over rise. Put the vertical change (4 - 8) on top and the horizontal change (60 - 20) on the bottom.
The size is right but the sign is not: the vertical value falls from 8 to 4 as the horizontal value rises, so the slope is negative.

items.q: A phone bill is $30 for 2 gigabytes of data and $50 for 6 gigabytes, on a straight line with gigabytes across and the bill up. By how many dollars does the bill rise for each extra gigabyte?

mistakes.why: That divides one point's values. Slope uses the CHANGES between two points: (50 - 30) over (6 - 2).

items.q: What is the slope of a horizontal line?
options: A negative number
The height of the line

items.q: Line P falls 3 units for every 1 unit across. Line Q falls 1 unit for every 3 units across. Which statement is correct?
options: Both slopes are negative, and Q is steeper
P has a positive slope and Q a negative one
They have the same slope because both fall
Both slopes are negative, and P is steeper

items.q: Along a straight line that falls to the right, how does the slope change as you move from left to right?
options: It becomes more negative
It stays the same
It becomes positive halfway along
It moves closer to 0

items.q: At what speed does the van reach the minimum point of its fuel curve?
options: 20 miles per hour
50 miles per hour
70 miles per hour
40 miles per hour

items.q: With speed across and fuel used up, what is the sign of the curve's slope between 20 and 40 miles per hour?
options: Positive, because both numbers in each row are positive
Zero, because the van keeps a steady speed
Positive, because the speed rises
Negative, because fuel used falls as speed rises

items.q: What is the slope of the fuel curve from 50 to 70 miles per hour, in gallons for each extra mile per hour of speed?

mistakes.why: That is run over rise. Divide the change in fuel (1.0) by the change in speed (20).

items.q: What does the table show about the slope of the fuel curve as speed rises from 20 to 70 miles per hour?
options: It is negative, reaches 0 near the minimum point, then turns positive
It is positive the whole way
It does not change from one speed to the next, as on a straight line
It is negative the whole way

items.q: Place point X on the downward-sloping curve D at a larger quantity than the point where D meets the upward-sloping curve S.
Place point Y on the upward-sloping curve S at a smaller quantity than the point where S meets D.
On a graph with price on the vertical axis, which change causes a movement along a curve rather than a shift of it?
options: A change in the number of buyers
A change in buyers' incomes
A change in the price of the good itself
A change in the cost of the sellers' materials

items.q: A curve "shifts right" on a graph with quantity across and price up. What does that mean?
options: At every price, the quantity is larger than before
At each quantity, the price is lower than before
The price rose and the quantity rose along the same curve
The curve became steeper

items.q: A new apartment building opens and at every price more people want to buy sandwiches at a deli. Shift the right curve the right way.

slips.S: The new building brings buyers, so it moves the buyers' curve D; a change in the deli's own costs would move S.

items.q: The flour a bakery buys becomes more expensive, so at every price the bakery offers fewer loaves. Shift the right curve the right way.

key.because: a rise in the cost of flour

slips.D: Flour is a cost for the bakery, so it moves the sellers' curve S, not the buyers' curve D.

items.q: A furniture maker buys a new saw that cuts twice as fast, so at every price it can offer more chairs. Shift the right curve the right way.

key.because: a faster saw that lowers costs

slips.D: The saw changes what the maker can offer, so it moves S; buyers want the same number of chairs as before at each price.

items.q: The price of movie tickets rises and nothing else changes. Place point X where buyers end up on the curve D.
A student says, "The price of bus fares fell, so the curve D for bus rides shifted right." What is wrong with the claim?
options: A lower fare shifts D left, not right
The fare is on the horizontal axis, so D stays put
Nothing is wrong: a lower fare shifts D right
A fare change is a movement along D, not a shift

items.q: On Monday the bakery cuts the price of a croissant from $4 to $3. How does its graph show this?
options: A shift of D to the right, at each price
A movement down along D
A shift of D to the left, at each price
A movement up along D to a smaller quantity

items.q: On Tuesday a large office opens next door. How does the graph show this?
options: A movement down along D, as after a price cut
D shifts right: more are wanted at each price
S shifts right: the bakery offers more at each price
D shifts left: fewer croissants are wanted at each price

items.q: On Thursday the butter the bakery buys doubles in price. How does the graph show this?
options: D shifts left: buyers want fewer croissants
A movement up along S to a larger quantity
S shifts right: the bakery offers more croissants at each price
S shifts left: fewer croissants offered at each price

items.q: On Friday a cafe across the street starts selling its own croissants for $2. What is the most likely change on Marlow Street Bakery's graph?
options: D shifts left: some buyers go to the cafe
D shifts right: customers want more croissants
A movement down along the curve D
S shifts left: the bakery bakes fewer croissants

items.q: Make the explanation specific: a cafe raises the price of its muffins and sells fewer. Fill in each blank.

specific.frame: The ___ changed, and it is the variable on ___, so the graph shows ___.

variable.label: What changed
options: price of muffins
number of buyers
cost of flour

why.1: Nothing in the scenario says the number of buyers changed; only the muffin price did.
why.2: The scenario changes the muffin price, not the cafe's costs.

axis.label: Which axis
options: the vertical axis
neither axis

why.1: Price is on the vertical axis of a market graph, so it is on an axis.

result.label: What the graph shows
options: a movement up along D
a shift of D to the left

why.1: A change in the good's own price never shifts D; buyers move along it to a smaller quantity.

specific.model: The price of muffins changed, and it is the variable on the vertical axis, so the graph shows a movement up along D to a smaller quantity, not a shift of the curve.

items.q: Put the steps for deciding between a shift and a movement in order.
options: Name what changed in the scenario
Check whether it is a variable on one of the axes
If it is, move along the curve; if not, shift the curve
For a shift, label the new curve 2 and draw an arrow

items.q: What is true at the point where two curves on a graph cross?
options: The two curves have the same slope there
The price is at its highest value on the graph
The point lies on both curves, so both share its price and quantity
The quantity is 0

items.q: In the graph, at what price and quantity do D and S cross?
options: $5 and 50 boxes
$10 and 0 boxes
$5 and 100 boxes
$50 and 5 boxes

items.q: What is the area of triangle A, which lies under D and above the $5 price, from 0 to 50 boxes?

mistakes.why: 250 is twice the triangle. Either you dropped the ½ (50 × 5 is the rectangle) or you measured the height from the axis (½ × 50 × 10). The height runs from $5 up to $10, which is 5, and a triangle is half of base × height: ½ × 50 × 5.
That drops the ½ and also measures the height from the axis. The triangle's height runs from $5 to $10 (5), and its area is ½ × 50 × 5.

items.q: What is the area of rectangle B, under the $5 price from 0 to 50 boxes?

mistakes.why: That halves the area, which is the rule for a triangle. B is a rectangle: base × height with no ½.

items.q: If D shifted right and the new crossing point were at $6 and 60 boxes, how would the new rectangle under the price, out to the quantity, compare with B?
options: It would be smaller, because D moved
It would be the same, 250
It would be larger: 60 × 6 ÷ 2 = 180
It would be larger: 60 × 6 = 360

items.q: More shoppers start coming to the market, so at every price buyers want more boxes of strawberries. Shift the right curve and mark the new crossing point.

slips.S: Shoppers are buyers, so they move D; S would move only if the farmers' costs or numbers changed.

items.q: A late frost damages the strawberry crop, so at every price farmers bring fewer boxes. Shift the right curve and mark the new crossing point.

key.because: a frost that damages the crop

slips.D: The frost changes what farmers can bring, so it moves S, not the buyers' curve D.

items.q: Shade the triangle that lies under the downward-sloping curve D and above the horizontal line through the crossing point, from 0 out to the crossing quantity.

slips.ps: That triangle sits BELOW the crossing price and above S. The one asked for sits above the price and under D.

items.q: Shade the triangle that lies above the upward-sloping curve S and below the horizontal line through the crossing point, from 0 out to the crossing quantity.

slips.cs: That triangle sits ABOVE the crossing price and under D. The one asked for sits below the price and above S.

items.q: A triangle on a graph has a base of 30 units along the quantity axis and a height of $8. What is its area, in dollars?

mistakes.why: That is the rectangle. A triangle with the same base and height is half of it.

items.q: A table shows that at $2 buyers want 70 bags and sellers offer 30; at $3, 60 and 45; at $4, 50 and 50; at $5, 40 and 55. At what price do the two curves cross?
The buyers' curve D shifts right and the sellers' curve S stays put. Along which curve does the crossing point move?
options: Along D, the curve that moved
Along S, the curve that did not move
Along neither: it stays where it was
Down the vertical axis

items.q: Put the steps for finding the area of a triangle on a graph in order.
options: Find the triangle's corners on the graph
Read its base along the horizontal axis
Read its height along the vertical axis
Multiply ½ × base × height
